standard_prerequisites.name: Numerical types, their genus and their Picard group
standard_prerequisites.statement: A numerical type is a collection of integers n, m of subscript i, a of subscript i j, w of subscript i and g of subscript i satisfying the symmetry and recurrence conditions of the chapter; the genus of the type is the alternating sum assembled from those integers and its Picard group is the cokernel of the matrix of divided intersection numbers, as in the neighbouring lemmas of the same section. Equivalence of numerical types and the operation of contracting a minus-one index are described in the same section; the author's own notation is retained inside the counted span.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma computes the Picard group for all types of genus at most zero, and it is the base of the induction that the following lemmas of the section use.

core_obligations: Induction on the number n of vertices of the type, with the case of a single vertex being immediate because the intersection matrix is then the zero matrix and the Picard group is the free module on one generator (source lines 1228-1229).

For n greater than one, use that a type of genus at most zero is not minimal, so that after replacing the type by an equivalent one there is an index whose weight and self-intersection make it a minus-one index, that is one eligible for contraction (source lines 1230-1232).

Contract that index: the Picard group of the contracted type contains the Picard group of the original one, and the genus is unchanged by the contraction, so the induction hypothesis applied to the contracted type, whose number of vertices is smaller, finishes the proof (source lines 1233-1238).

proof_roadmap.step: Base of the induction: a single-vertex type has zero intersection matrix, hence Picard group the integers.
Non-minimality of a type of genus at most zero, and the reduction to a type carrying an index eligible for contraction.
Contract the index, compare the two Picard groups, note that the genus is unchanged and conclude by induction.
